question: Over four weeks an index falls from 3,500 to 2,800. Spot VIX rises from 16 to 48, the front-month VIX future from 16 to 42, and a near-dated VIX call from $0.40 to $10.40. Roughly how many times larger was the call's percentage gain than spot VIX's percentage gain?
options: About 3x
About 8x
About 12.5x
About 26x

question: Spot VIX holds steady at 15 for a month. A trader bought the front-month VIX future at 18.0 at the start of the month and holds it to settlement. What is the percentage return?
During a crisis, spot VIX is 35 and the front-month future is 31. If spot VIX stays at 35 through expiration, what return does a long position in that future earn?
A VIX call bought for $0.50 gains 3,000% during a volatility spike. What is its new price?
An exchange-traded product holds a short position in short-term VIX futures, rebalanced daily. Over a long period dominated by contango with occasional spikes, what pattern is most likely?
options: Steady losses with occasional large gains in spikes
A price that tracks spot VIX one-for-one over time
Gradual roll gains punctuated by sharp losses in spikes
Gains in all conditions, with no exposure to spikes

question: A long VIX futures fund loses about 5% of its value to contango roll each month while spot VIX stays roughly unchanged. Compounded over 12 months, approximately what cumulative loss results?
VIX futures carry a $1,000 multiplier per index point. A trader long one contract sees the price rise from 18.00 to 26.00. What is the gain?

A $10 million portfolio wants VIX calls that pay about $1 million in total if the VIX settles at 40. Each call contract would pay $2,000 at that level and costs $120 today. What is the approximate upfront cost?
A $5 million equity portfolio falls 20% in a crash. Separately, VIX calls bought for $50,000 are worth $650,000 at the low. What is the net change relative to the $5 million?
In the VXTH strategy, what is the portfolio weight allocation when front-month VIX futures trade below 15?
Apart from rising implied volatility, what option feature makes an out-of-the-money VIX call's gains accelerate as the VIX keeps climbing?
options: Its delta stays fixed at 0.30 as the VIX rises
Time decay adds to its value as the spike unfolds
Positive gamma: its delta rises toward 1 as it goes in the money
Its vega falls to zero as the VIX rises, removing drag

question: A manager keeps 1% of the portfolio in one-month VIX calls every month regardless of conditions. In a calm year, 10 of the 12 monthly purchases expire worthless and the other two just return their cost. Roughly what is the annual drag on returns?

The index is at 4,200. An investor buys a 4,000-strike put for 50 points to protect a long index position. Ignoring other costs, what index level at expiration is needed for the hedged position to break even?
An index is at 3,000. An investor holding it buys a 2,850 put for 45 and sells a 3,150 call for 45. If the index ends at 2,600 at expiration, what is the hedged return?

An index is at 4,000. A zero-cost collar of the CLLZ type buys a 3,900 put, sells a 3,800 put and sells a call above the market, for zero net premium. If the index ends at 3,500, what is the hedged return?
Why do protective put and collar programs usually show a lower beta to the S&P 500 than buy-and-hold?
options: They hold fewer shares than a buy-and-hold position
Their options damp the index's moves in both directions
Their short calls add leverage when the index rallies
They hold VIX futures, which carry a negative beta

question: The risk-free rate is 2%. A collar program returns 6% with 9% standard deviation; buy-and-hold returns 9% with 15% standard deviation. Which has the higher Sharpe ratio?
options: The collar, 0.67 vs 0.60
Buy-and-hold, 0.47 vs 0.44
The collar, 0.47 vs 0.44
They are equal

question: A hedger compares VIX calls struck at 20 and at 30 when the front-month future is 17. What is the main trade-off of choosing the 30 strike?
options: It costs more but pays off in smaller volatility spikes
It pays off sooner because it is further out-of-the-money
It is cheaper but needs a much larger spike to pay off
It removes basis risk relative to the 20-strike call

question: In a calm, slowly rising market, what is the main ongoing cost of continuously holding protective options?
options: Margin calls on the long options
Time decay of the option premiums as they approach expiry
Lost dividends on the index
Rising implied volatility lifting the premiums

question: A portfolio holds 95% in the index and 5% in short-term VIX futures. In one week the index falls 4% and the VIX futures gain 30%. What is the portfolio's return?
A one-month at-the-money S&P 500 put costs 2.0% of the index. With implied volatility unchanged, roughly what would a three-month at-the-money put cost?

An investor holds a 3,800 SPX put after the index rallied to 4,400; the put is now worth 5. To keep protection about 5% below the market, the investor sells it and buys a 4,180 put for 55. What is the net cost of this roll?
Over six months the S&P 500 declines 15% in a slow grind while the VIX rises only from 15 to 20. Which hedge most likely performed better?
options: OTM VIX calls, because any decline makes them soar
VIX calls, because the VIX and S&P 500 move inversely
S&P 500 puts, because they pay on the index level itself
VIX futures held through the contango period

question: A hedger buys a VIX 20 call for 1.80 and sells a VIX 35 call for 0.50 with the same expiration. What is the maximum profit per unit at expiration?
An investor owns the index at 4,000 and sells a 4,100 call for 60 (a buy-write). If the index ends at 3,700, what is the position's loss as a percentage of 4,000?
Why do buy-write (covered call) and put-write programs not function as tail-risk hedges?
options: They need VIX futures to implement and roll
They are long volatility, so they lag in calm markets
They cap losses at the strike of the option sold
They are short volatility and keep most crash losses

question: An investor wants a fixed floor under an S&P 500 holding and refuses to cap upside. Which hedge fits best?
options: A zero-cost collar
A buy-write
A protective SPX put bought outright
A short VIX futures position

question: A $2.4 million portfolio moves one-for-one with the S&P 500 (beta 1.0). The index is at 4,800 and SPX options have a $100 multiplier. How many put contracts are needed to cover the portfolio's notional value?
In the VXTH design, what happens to the VIX calls when they reach expiration?
options: The position is closed and VIX futures are bought instead
They are held until the VIX future crosses 50
The strategy waits a full quarter before buying again
They are rolled into new one-month 30-delta VIX calls

question: Which pair names two option-based methods for protecting a long S&P 500 portfolio against downside risk?
options: Selling SPX puts and selling VIX calls
Buying SPX calls and selling VIX puts
Buying VIX calls and buying SPX puts
Selling SPX calls and buying VIX puts
